solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: A portion of blancmange, a syllabub, and a piece of cake (4)

indicatorNotes.A portion of: the answer is only a portion of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A plate of pudding: some blancmange, some syllabub and a slice of cake.
annotation.walkthrough: The list of desserts makes 'a piece of cake' look like one more item on the plate, but it is the idiom for something simple. A syllabub is a whipped cream-and-wine pudding.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a piece of cake is any task that takes no effort.

entries.clue: Posh bloke’s papa leaving something inside oyster? (4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: papa's letter leaves the word, so it is removed

blocks.note: a pearl grows inside an oyster; the question mark flags the definition by example
Papa is the radio code word for P; drop it from PEARL

annotation.surface: A gentleman's father has left, as if leaving the inside of an oyster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Posh bloke’s' reads as a possessive, but the ’s is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a peer of the realm is the archetypal posh bloke.

entries.clue: Advocate spreading soil about with this object before worm’s discovered (9)

indicatorNotes.spreading: the letters of soil are spread out into a new order
indicatorNotes.before: the IT group comes before the last piece
indicatorNotes.discovered: dis-covered: the worm loses its covering, its outside letters

blocks.note: wORm without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A gardener's instruction: spread soil around this thing before the worm turns up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' means found in the surface but uncovered in the wordplay: WORM loses its outer letters. Solicitor is the British name for a lawyer who handles clients' affairs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are lawyers who plead a client's cause.

entries.clue: In favour of strike the steward finally put forward (10)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the final letter of each of the two words

annotation.surface: A union meeting: a steward finally speaks up in favour of a strike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finally' covers both words before it, not just 'steward'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: offering a theory up for debate, in a formal register.

entries.clue: Parts of a building fell over on top of someone (5)

indicatorNotes.over: the word is turned over, read backwards
indicatorNotes.on: in a down entry, one piece sits on top of the next
indicatorNotes.top of: the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a fell is a moor, upland in northern England; MOOR backwards

annotation.surface: A building collapses and something falls on a person underneath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past of fall, but it is the noun: a fell is a hill or moor in the north of England.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the spaces that a building's walls divide it into.

entries.clue: Put back letters called, but leave out H (9)

indicatorNotes.leave out: the H is left out of the word before it

annotation.surface: Someone telephones, puts the letters back and is told to skip the H.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reads as returning something to its place, but here it means moving to a later date.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting a meeting back moves it to a later date.

entries.clue: Loosen the middle of spinnaker taken in by us sailors (7)

indicatorNotes.the middle of: the central letter of the nine-letter word
indicatorNotes.taken in by: to be taken in by something is to be received inside it, so the N ends up within US

blocks.note: spinNaker: N is the fifth of nine letters
a crew = the sailors of a ship

annotation.surface: Sailors letting the middle of their spinnaker sail go slack.
annotation.walkthrough: The sailing picture makes 'loosen' sound like easing a sail, but it is turning a screw the other way.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific case: turning a threaded cap or bolt anticlockwise is one way of loosening it.

entries.clue: Question: do you bet on vacation? (5)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: the word is vacated, emptied of its middle

annotation.surface: A question for a traveller: do you gamble while on holiday?
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark makes the whole clue look like a question, while 'Question' is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to be unsure whether a claim is true.

entries.clue: Unkempt detective inspector’s given instructions (10)

blocks.note: DI = detective inspector, a British police rank

annotation.surface: A scruffy police detective has been given his orders.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts 'Unkempt' on the detective, but it stands apart as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: untidy, in a mess, as hair or a room can be.

entries.clue: Refuse to look at topless foreign dances (6)

indicatorNotes.topless: the word loses its top, its first letter
indicatorNotes.dances: the remaining letters dance into a new order

annotation.surface: A prude averts their eyes from topless dancers abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foreign dances' looks like the thing refused, but 'foreign' is the fodder and 'dances' the instruction to rearrange it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: deliberately paying something no attention.

entries.clue: Conscientious US soldier drills crude US oil with army engineers (9)

indicatorNotes.drills: the soldier drills into the letters, ending up inside them
indicatorNotes.crude: crude oil is unrefined, so its letters are in raw order

blocks.note: RE = Royal Engineers, the British army's engineer corps
GI = American soldier; goes between LI and OUS

annotation.surface: An American soldier and army engineers drill for crude oil.
annotation.walkthrough: The oilfield picture makes 'drills' look literal; it is the containment, with GI boring into the rearranged US OIL.
annotation.definitionFit: A secondary sense: doing something with religious care means doing it scrupulously.

entries.clue: Foam-smothered soft potatoes (5)

indicatorNotes.smothered: the foam smothers, covers all around, the soft letter

blocks.note: p = piano, soft in music; goes inside SUDS

annotation.surface: Soft potatoes smothered in a frothy topping.
annotation.walkthrough: In the surface 'soft' describes the potatoes; in the wordplay it is the P that the suds wrap.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British and Irish slang for the vegetable.

entries.clue: Evocation of bygone days in Czechoslovakia (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the word that follows

annotation.surface: Nostalgia for the old days of Czechoslovakia, a country that no longer exists.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Czechoslovakia itself belongs to bygone days, split into Czechia and Slovakia in 1993.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a reminder of the past is a reverberation of it.

entries.clue: One really famous South American going around a pitch (9)

indicatorNotes.going around: US goes around PER, holding it inside

blocks.note: a = per, as in ten pounds a head
pitch = tar, the black sticky stuff

annotation.surface: A famous South American footballer runs around the pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one word, a Brazilian star perhaps, but it splits into S and US. 'Pitch' looks like the football field; it is tar.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a celebrity of the very first rank.

entries.clue: A pale rope surrounding helipad that indicates ownership (10)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for 'something that indicates ownership'

indicatorNotes.surrounding: a rope surrounding something encircles it, so the rope's letters close around the H

blocks.note: a pale is a fence stake, a post
H marks a helipad; it goes inside ROPE

annotation.surface: A pale-coloured rope ringing a helipad, as a boundary marking private property.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pale' looks like a colour, but it is the noun: a stake in a fence. The H painted on a helipad gives H.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the punctuation mark in John's shows possession.

entries.clue: One boring open-and-shut case (7)

indicatorNotes.boring: the I bores into the word, ending up inside it

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral; goes inside PATENT

annotation.surface: A dull person, and a legal case that is easy to settle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Open-and-shut case' reads as one phrase, but 'case' is split off as the definition: a doctor's case is a patient. A dentist's patient is also bored in a different sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical sense: doctors call a person under their care a case.

entries.clue: Leaders of the regiment upset soldiers before tense operation? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the question mark flags an operation as one example of treatment

indicatorNotes.Leaders of: the leading letters of the words that follow
indicatorNotes.before: the soldiers come before the T

blocks.note: to eat someone is to upset them: what's eating you?

annotation.surface: The regiment's commanders are upset that their troops face a nervous military operation.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'operation' military and 'tense' nervous; they are a surgical operation and the grammar abbreviation T.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: surgery is one kind of medical care.

entries.clue: In this time and in this place or not in any place (7)

annotation.surface: A riddle about being here and now, or nowhere at all.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'now' and 'here' together make their opposite. 'Or' here only links wordplay and definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: not anywhere at all.

entries.clue: Shoplifter damaged case left at the back of Costco close to Chester (9)

indicatorNotes.damaged: the letters of case are damaged into a new order
indicatorNotes.the back of: the last letter of the word
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: A shoplifter's broken case left behind a Costco near Chester.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shoplifter' is not a thief: it is something in a shop that lifts people between floors.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: a moving staircase lifts shoppers between floors, so it is literally a shop lifter.

entries.clue: Cook unshelled heron eggs (3)

indicatorNotes.unshelled: the word loses its shell, its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.Cook: the remaining letters are cooked into a new order

annotation.surface: A recipe: cook the eggs of a heron after peeling them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heron eggs' reads as one thing to cook; the heron is the fodder and 'eggs' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fish eggs eaten as food.

entries.clue: Higgs, for example, articulated the Large Hadron Collider objective (7)

indicatorNotes.articulated: the words are spoken, so we go by their sound

blocks.note: the collider belongs to CERN, and its aim is its objective

annotation.surface: Peter Higgs spells out what the Large Hadron Collider was built to find.
annotation.walkthrough: The collider was built to find the Higgs boson, so 'Higgs' looks like part of the physics; it is simply an example of a family name. CERN is the European physics lab near Geneva that runs the collider.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Higgs is a family name, Peter Higgs's.

entries.clue: Suspect evacuated Leningrad a year before the time in question (7)

indicatorNotes.evacuated: the word is emptied, keeping only its outer letters
indicatorNotes.Suspect: the letters are suspect, not in their proper order

annotation.surface: A suspect evacuated from wartime Leningrad a year before the period being investigated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evacuated' fits the siege of Leningrad, but it means emptied out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: by then, earlier than the moment under discussion.

entries.clue: Editor put about explosive cable, causing fiasco (7)

indicatorNotes.explosive: the letters are blown apart into a new order

annotation.surface: An editor sends out an inflammatory telegram and a disaster follows.
annotation.walkthrough: A cable is a telegram, so the surface is an editor's explosive message.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean a humiliating collapse.

entries.clue: BA Baracus’s head is cut by 12 bits of litter? (6)

annotation.definitionNote: the question mark flags the pun: a litter is a brood of young animals

indicatorNotes.head: the head of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.cut by: IS is cut open by the E, which sits inside it

blocks.note: 12 across is ECHO, the radio code word for E; it cuts IS

annotation.surface: B. A. Baracus of The A-Team takes a head wound from flying rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: B. A. Baracus is Mr T's character in The A-Team. The cross-reference to 12 is ECHO, and Echo is the radio code word for E.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun: a litter is a brood of newborn animals, and each member is a young one.

entries.clue: Strong coffee, stirred endlessly, boiled two times over (9)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: the word loses its end, its last letter
indicatorNotes.boiled: the remaining letters boil into a new order

blocks.note: STIRRED minus its final D, rearranged

annotation.surface: Making strong coffee: stir it constantly and boil it twice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stirred' belongs with coffee in the surface, but it is the fodder, and 'boiled' is the instruction to mix it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short, extra-concentrated espresso shot.

entries.clue: Lively hedgehog back at home among green leaves (5)

indicatorNotes.back: the finished group is read back to front
indicatorNotes.among: IN goes among the letters of COS

blocks.note: cos is a crisp green lettuce, romaine in America
in = at home; goes inside COS to make CINOS

annotation.surface: A hedgehog perks up back home among the leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: Sonic the Hedgehog is the fast blue video-game character, so 'Lively hedgehog' is the definition as a whole.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: Sega's video-game hedgehog is famous for his speed.

entries.clue: Multilayered tearjerker being performed twice, overwhelming yours truly (5)

indicatorNotes.twice: the word is used two times
indicatorNotes.overwhelming: the two ONs overwhelm the I, closing around it

blocks.note: on = being performed, as a show is on; twice
yours truly = I, the setter; goes between the two ONs

annotation.surface: A layered weepie of a play so good it runs twice and overwhelms me.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tearjerker' sounds like a sad film; an onion makes you cry when you cut it, and it is made of layers.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the vegetable grows in layers and makes you cry when you cut it.

entries.clue: Cow’s tail removed for tripe (4)

indicatorNotes.tail removed: the word's tail, its last letter, is taken off

blocks.note: to cow = to bully; the ’s is 'is'; drop the Y

annotation.surface: Cutting the tail off a cow to make tripe.
annotation.walkthrough: The butcher's scene makes 'cow' an animal and 'tripe' offal; they are the verb 'to cow' and tripe meaning nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang synonyms: both mean nonsense.

entries.clue: Disown golden yellow trousers (4)

indicatorNotes.trousers: to trouser is to pocket, so the phrase pockets the answer

annotation.surface: Refusing to own up to a pair of golden yellow trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' is a verb, not the garment: to trouser is British slang for to pocket.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: refusing to acknowledge someone as your own.

entries.clue: Animal from the remotest parts of Patagonia (5)

annotation.definition: Animal from the remotest parts of Patagonia

blocks.note: the surface reading: a creature native to somewhere
the surface wants the far south of Argentina; read literally, the word's remotest parts are its first and last letters, joined by 'and'

annotation.surface: A wild creature from the far corners of South America.
annotation.walkthrough: Pandas live in China, not Patagonia, which is the joke: the outermost letters of Patagonia are P and A, spelt out as 'P and A'.
annotation.definitionFit: A whole-clue reading: 'animal' is the plain category, and the rest spells the name out from the two outermost letters of the place.

entries.clue: Most important part of long film course cut short (9)

indicatorNotes.cut short: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: an epic is a long, big-scale film
an entrée is a course of a meal; drop the last E

annotation.surface: The key scene of a long film is trimmed down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Course' sounds like a route or class, but it is a course of a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the point above an earthquake's focus, extended to the heart of anything.

entries.clue: Trying child’s first pen out? Is this what I’m doing? (10)

indicatorNotes.first: the first letter of the word
indicatorNotes.out: the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: A parent frets over a tiresome child whose pen has run out, then the setter muses on the job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like an adjective for the child; it is fodder. The definition is the setter asking whether they are encrypting, which is what setting a cryptic crossword is.
annotation.definitionFit: A self-reference: the setter is hiding words in code by writing cryptic clues.

entries.clue: King George ‘the Old’ turns pale (4)

indicatorNotes.turns: the phrase turns round, read backwards

blocks.note: ye = the, in olde-style spelling such as Ye Olde Shoppe

annotation.surface: An ageing King George, called 'the Old', goes pale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The Old' looks like a royal nickname; it asks for the old form of 'the', which is YE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ashen and colourless, as a sick face is.
